text: Sustainability in Quality Improvement: Outcomes of a Novel Pediatric Virtual Urgent Care in Ontario, Canada. Virtual care is expected to play an increasingly important role in the Canadian healthcare system, with the 2023-2024 Health Canada Departmental Plan outlining the advancement of digital health solutions as a focal point. However, key outcomes of transitioning from traditional in-person healthcare appointments to a virtual model of care are not yet well-described. Here, we apply the Sustainability in Quality Improvement (SusQI) framework to patients seen in a novel pediatric virtual urgent care (VUC) program to quantify the environmental, economic, and social impacts of virtual care.

Meta-analysis of 990 EBV genomes identifies EBER2 SNP7048 and its interaction with HLA-A*11:01 driving nasopharyngeal carcinoma risk. Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a major health burden in East and Southeast Asia (SEA). While EBV infection is a primary driver, the specific viral strains responsible for NPC development and their interaction with host genetics across geographically diverse endemic regions remain poorly understood. We performed a whole-genome sequencing of 388 EBV isolates and matched host whole-exome sequencing in a Singaporean cohort. To define the global significance of these findings, we conducted a meta-GWAS and phylogenetic analysis across three independent cohorts (Singapore, Hong Kong, and Guangdong and Guangxi provinces of China), totaling 990 EBV genomes. Our study identifies high-risk EBV strains-carrying a core variant in the EBER2 locus (SNP7048)-as the key viral determinator of NPC risk, accounting for approximately 68% of the attributable risk in SEA. Meta-analysis reveals these strains are consistently associated with NPC across all populations, resolving previous regional genetic discordances. We demonstrate a potent synergistic interaction between these EBV risk strains and the host HLA-A*11:01 protective allele; individuals lacking this protection while carrying a high-risk strain exhibit a 30.9-fold increase in NPC risk. Phylogenetic analysis further reveals that these high-risk lineages populated SEA through clonal expansion from Southern China, following historical migration routes. These findings establish that NPC development is driven by the distribution of specific high-risk EBV lineages and their synergistic interaction with host immune susceptibility. This provides a definitive genetic framework for precision population screening and early diagnosis of NPC in the endemic regions.

A Mandarin Speech Intelligibility Prediction Model for Hearing Aids. Objective speech intelligibility prediction methods provide a low-cost alternative to tests with human listeners, allowing the investigation of many factors affecting intelligibility. However, the objective prediction of speech intelligibility for Mandarin-speaking listeners with hearing impairment is largely underdeveloped. Existing intelligibility metrics are based on English linguistic structures and/or are designed primarily for normal-hearing listeners. This paper introduces a Mandarin Chinese Hearing-Aid Speech Perception Index (MCHASPI), an objective metric for predicting the intelligibility of speech processed by hearing aids for Mandarin Chinese speakers with or without hearing loss. A key challenge was the scarcity of high-quality datasets and the lack of models tailored to the perceptual characteristics of Mandarin Chinese. To address this, we first constructed a Mandarin intelligibility dataset using subjective hearing tests, for speech with six types of distortions. A hearing loss simulator was employed to preprocess the reference (undistorted) and test speech signals. Multiple features were extracted from these processed signals and combined for subsequent analysis. Two prediction models were developed, namely MCHASPI-NN and MCHASPI-L, utilizing a neural network and a logistic mapping function, respectively, to predict intelligibility from feature values. The core of the MCHASPI model involves a perceptually motivated segmental stretching scheme for precise signal alignment, followed by frame-wise threshold detection and multi-feature fusion. Evaluations with normal-hearing and hearing-impaired listeners demonstrated that MCHASPI gave significantly more accurate predictions than existing models across all tested datasets. This validates the effectiveness of MCHASPI for assessing Mandarin speech intelligibility for populations with varying degrees of hearing loss.

Spectrotemporal Processing Using the Spectral-Temporally Modulated Ripple Test and Its Relation to Cognition and Hearing Loss in Adults. The three-alternative forced-choice design of the spectral-temporally modulated ripple test (SMRT) may capture both auditory and neurocognitive functioning. The relationships between neurocognitive functions and SMRT performance remain unexplored in middle-aged and older adults, as does the degree to which hearing loss may affect these relationships. This study hypothesized that better neurocognitive functions and better hearing would predict better SMRT performance and that hearing loss and neurocognitive functions would interact in contributing to SMRT performance.
